The Atlanta Fed’s Q4 real GDP tracker though eased to +3.38%, the least since its +3.22% initiation on October 29th, down from +3.48% on November 9th.

The biggest move since the last update was a -0.15% drop in the contribution from residential investment (to -0.12% from +0.03%), mostly after last Wednesday’s existing home sales report. 

Consumption's contribution also fell -0.07% (to +1.72% from +1.79%), mostly after today’s reports (which looks strange given the strength of the control group, but the model actually raised its goods spending estimate; the drag came from services, led by a plunge in October utility spending in today’s industrial production data and a drop in restaurant sales; also September retail spending was revised up giving a higher compare). Those were partly offset by gains in inventories (+0.09%) and government spending (+0.06%).

As a reminder, the Atlanta Fed’s tracker started very strong in each of Q1, Q2 and Q3 before falling sharply as we approached the actual GDP reads: Q1 went from 3.13% to 1.99%, Q2 from 3.70% to 1.50%, and Q3 from 4.95% to 3.37%. We're far from that point, though, as we won't get the Q4 report until late January.

The reading for now remains well above the blue chip consensus* of ~+2.1%.

Here’s the breakdown of the components as of November 17th and changes from my last update November 9th:

Consumption = +1.72% (-0.07%)

Nonresidential fixed investment (biz spending) = +1.35% (-0.04%)

Inventories = +0.61% (+0.09%)

Gov’t = +0.27% (+0.06%)

Residential investment = -0.12% (-0.15%)

Net exports = -0.46% (0.00%)

GDPNow Forecast: +3.38% (-0.10%)

Boring Company CEO Steve Davis says he'll retire "the day I can commute from D.C. to Vegas in half an hour."

That would mean traveling more than 4,000 miles an hour. But before it can build a hyperloop, the Boring Company has to make tunnels cheap.

Since its founding in 2017, the company has brought tunneling costs below $10 million a mile. Davis expects that to fall to $4 million to $5 million, less than adding a lane to many urban highways.

"If we're below $5 million," Davis asks, "why would you ever build a road again?"

The most important consequence of this underground future may be the cost to access a city.

If a two-hour commute drops to ten minutes, inexpensive land far from the city could become a practical place to build homes. Eventually, tunnels could connect cities too.

"You can solve the rent and cost of living problem by making all of these places very desirable to live with just transportation," Davis says.

It's officially Nvidia's earnings day.

Today's earnings report and call will likely be the most watched earnings event in history.

We are watching two key things:

1. Do executives show any willingness to reinstate Jensen Huang

2. What has CHANGED from a business perspective

As of now, considering the information over the last 48 hours, we believe there is an <20% chance that Jensen returns.

Any indication that the probability is higher would be strongly bullish for the stock.

But, if not, then what has changed for Nvidia? With or without Jensen, this company remains one of the best businesses in the world.

We are looking to see if the company still expects revenue growth of 70%+ in FY2028, as management previously indicated.

We also look for any changes to AI infrastructure spending, demand for Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips, and the company's relationships with its largest customers.

If the fundamental outlook remains intact, then investors must ask: Does Jensen Huang's departure justify the -$750 billion in lost market cap?

We believe the market has already priced in a significant portion of the uncertainty surrounding Jensen's departure.

At the same time, the long-term AI infrastructure investment cycle remains intact, and Nvidia continues to sit at the center of it.

The burden is now on management to demonstrate that the business can continue executing at the same level without Jensen Huang.

More to come after earnings.

The off ramping we are seeing is not bullish. There's no way to spin that. 

My guess is that this decline still has a way to go. Anywhere from 6-9 months until stablecoins start to inflect upwards again looking at 2022, but it’s impossible to forecast as it will be linked to the progress of AI.

Stablecoins declining is one of the strongest indicators we have for prolonged bearish PA. It is not necessarily a predictor of a bottom, just that things don't go up much.

I think the anxiety right now of self custody, DEXs and CEXs is too much in general for everyone (normal investors and OGs alike). And it is entirely rational. The surface area of risk has increased due to the new powers that hackers have.

Lighter has lost 100M TVL in the last couple of days, and that spook event for a major name will see people continually reduce exposure to perps dexs for the time being. Hyperliquid has lost 8.82% of their stablecoins in the last 7 days.

I don’t like saying bearish things, but I have survived many cycles by being hyper aware of increased risks. You should be employing the horcrux method and making sure you haven't got too much exposure to one venue. 

Once onchain comes out on the other side of this the systems will be almost impenetrable, which will be a very good thing long term, but that hardening can only come with time and by the best security teams reacting to the increasing complexity of attacks and recognising that every layer of the stack can be a weak point.

Perps platforms are still going to do extraordinarily well once we move past the "everything is going to get hacked" stage, and they are still the thing I am most bullish on.

Always prioritise survival so you can continually play another hand.

Perps platforms are still going to do extraordinarily well once we move past the "everything is going to get hacked" stage, and they are still the thing I am most bullish on.

Always prioritise survival so you can continually play another hand.

#Uranium #Nuclear $M.CN $MYRUF

The uranium deficit has a timing problem: utilities can increase their bids overnight. New mines take years.

Mined uranium covered just 90% of reactor requirements in 2024, with secondary supplies bridging the gap. Meanwhile, the World Nuclear Association’s reference scenario projects uranium requirements more than doubling between 2025 and 2040. Closing that gap requires investment and new production.

That is what makes Myriad Uranium’s below presentation worth watching.

At Copper Mountain in Wyoming, approximately 2,000 historical drill holes provide a substantial foundation for exploration. Myriad’s Phase II programme is working to verify historical deposits, support a maiden current resource estimate and test additional targets.

One detail particularly caught my attention: at Canning, chemical assay grades averaged 60% above gamma-probe equivalents at the 1,000 ppm cutoff. That raises an intriguing possibility that some earlier measurements understated the uranium present. The impact on a future resource still needs to be established.

There is also a strategic dimension: only 7% of uranium delivered to U.S. nuclear plants in 2025 was U.S.-origin material. Developing domestic supply could become increasingly valuable as energy security moves up the agenda. Myriad has potentially the largest uranium project in the U.S.

A few people read my recent post as a sign I’m no longer bullish on #uranium.

Nothing could be further from the truth.

I’m still as bullish as ever. This equity wipeout risks delaying financing for the very projects needed to meet future demand. The longer new supply gets pushed back, the more explosive the eventual price response will be.

When utilities start questioning whether there will be enough fuel for everyone, securing pounds will matter far more than the price paid.

I still believe uranium will trade well above $200/lb and that we will se many equities go 10x and more from current levels.

But a strong long-term thesis doesn’t protect a small sector from tax-loss selling and ETF rebalancing. Understanding those flows can make a huge difference to your portfolio.

That does NOT mean I think you should sell now if you didn’t earlier. We may already be close to the lows, even with further tax-loss selling still possible.

Canada could take a lesson from Sweden’s ISK system, where investors generally pay an annual tax based on account value rather than tax on each realised gain. That removes the same incentive to dump losing positions simply to crystallise a tax loss.

In my view, tax-driven selling creates unnecessary market distortions. But until the rules change, it makes sense to understand them and adapt.

Being bullish on uranium and being tactical with uranium equities are perfectly compatible.

That does NOT mean I think you should sell now if you didn’t earlier. We may already be close to the lows, even with further tax-loss selling still possible.

Canada could take a lesson from Sweden’s ISK system, where investors generally pay an annual tax based on account value rather than tax on each realised gain. That removes the same incentive to dump losing positions simply to crystallise a tax loss.

In my view, tax-driven selling creates unnecessary market distortions. But until the rules change, it makes sense to understand them and adapt.

Being bullish on uranium and being tactical with uranium equities are perfectly compatible.

$NVDA earnings preview: I expect the 
stock to drift down into the print. Expect to hear less than you want. 

What we could hear:
•  Impact of the blue wave on data center builds.
•  A framework to estimate the impact of yesterday’s Commerce Department’s new license requirements for Remote Access to American Super Intelligence Technology. My sense is at most 10% of revenue could be impacted.

What we likely won’t hear:
•  Updates on the CEO search. Anything on culture. 
•  Guidance.
•  Updates on the future of Nvidia-led datacenter financing.

What could cause the stock to drop:
•  Comments that the business needs to be overhauled.

What could cause it to trade higher:
While we likely won’t get guidance, strong better-than-95% YoY growth (vs. Street at 91%) for the October revenue and stable gross margins around 74%could lead investors to remember that demand for their GPUs is strong and the tailwinds remain healthy.

Whenever I make a major investment error, I spend a considerable amount of time dissecting everything that led to it.

Not just the fundamental assumptions that turned out to be wrong, but also my psychological state at the time. How much greed, fear, overconfidence, or other emotions influenced my judgment. Where I got my information, why I considered those sources credible, and why I interpreted that information the way I did.

The goal isn’t just to understand what went wrong, but to understand exactly how my thinking and decision-making process led me to that conclusion, and how I can prevent it from happening again.

That’s why I rarely make the same investment error twice.

I think we can all agree that NVIDIA will deliver strong results, and I expect the business to continue performing exceptionally well over the next couple of years.

The cloud hanging over $NVDA is the Jensen Huang situation, and another great earnings report isn’t going to resolve it.

In my view, the only real market catalyst this week that could de-risk the entire AI trade is a successful Anthropic ($ANT) IPO on Thursday.

If the IPO goes exceptionally well, I wouldn’t be surprised to see the Nasdaq rally 3% in response. It could restore confidence across the entire AI sector.

And for those who like to bet on short-term moves, I wouldn’t be surprised to see both $NBIS (Nebius) and $CRWV (CoreWeave) rally 20% by the end of the week following a successful Anthropic IPO.

Podcasts, TV shows, and seemingly everyone on Wall Street and X were celebrating Leopold Aschenbrenner as the new wunderkind, the genius who had supposedly figured out Wall Street and the future of AI.

Now, with hindsight, it’s easy for everyone to see the risks. But at the time, I was almost the only voice on X warning people to be extremely careful with this guy. His returns seemed astronomical, almost illogical. Something about the numbers simply didn’t add up.

For saying that, I received countless hate messages telling me how stupid I was, that I didn’t understand his genius, and that I was simply jealous of his success. Interestingly, looking back at my original post now, I see that most of those comments have conveniently been deleted. Typical X behavior.

I’m not jealous of anyone’s success. I wish everyone great success. But one thing I’m very good at is recognizing patterns.

Only in hindsight did we discover the extraordinary leverage behind those returns. Reports indicated that his fund was borrowing as much as $3 to $4 for every $1 of capital. What appeared to be extraordinary investment genius was also extraordinary risk-taking.

According to CNBC, Aschenbrenner’s hedge fund, Situational Awareness, reached $45 billion in assets at its peak before declining to around $10 billion. Its latest 13F shows just $1.58 billion in disclosed U.S. securities, although that figure does not represent the fund’s total assets.

And this goes far beyond Aschenbrenner. Just look at the latest 13F filings. Some of the most respected hedge funds on Wall Street were loading up on AI-related stocks, including $NVDA, during the third quarter, just before the recent selloff.

These are supposed to be the smartest people in the room, surrounded by the best analysts, researchers, and resources money can buy. Yet many were heavily exposed to the very sector that subsequently collapsed.

That’s the point. Nobody has a crystal ball. There are no saviors.

There is no Wall Street genius who has cracked the market. No AI wunderkind who has discovered the secret to investing. No growth stock promoter selling you a shortcut to becoming rich.

There is a reason not everyone is wealthy. Generating exceptional investment returns consistently over long periods is extraordinarily difficult. That’s how markets work.

Never confuse a short-term track record with genuine investment skill.

Someone who wins the lottery doesn’t suddenly become the smartest person in the room. And someone who delivers three spectacular years of returns hasn’t necessarily figured out Wall Street.

Time is the ultimate test. Not podcasts, not followers, not headlines, and certainly not three years of performance.

Indian law enforcement froze $3M from an innocent Chinese investor after mistaking a crypto bridge for a pig butchering scam. Now an Indian court has ordered Gate to hand his funds to a person they never belonged to.

My analysis of how Indian LE traced through an unlabeled service and wrongly froze @xxxkeym's Gate account:

The case stems from a pig butchering victim who allegedly lost $1.7M of BTC, USDT, DOGE & SOL in May 2025.

Andhra Pradesh CID registered it as Cr. No. 10/2025 and filed a charge sheet in March 2026.

In July 2025, xxxkeym had Gate deposit address 17mpajZ6Nq3dG3T6wUhaXxYF4Qy9HJnYx5 frozen after depositing 15 BTC from 3NcBhqK in the following transaction:
885f3afab562251b222363cf12095e864ddb94636674b01f0cdb05997e5a54a0

This is one transaction Indian LE cites in its notice. 3NcBhqK was funded by xxxkeym's own OKX & Binance withdrawals in Jan 2023 and the coins sat dormant for years until the Gate deposit. 

Indian LE never froze his OKX or Binance accounts, the actual source of the 15 BTC, which tells you how flawed their justification is.

Gate froze his entire account, which held roughly $3M at the time and about $1.5M today.

The Indian court order hands all of it to the complainant.

Gate deposit address 17mpajZ also received two deposits for 15 BTC total in 2025 from bc1pkkwqyxn3rm608ryuqg9hyqna0syq4jx5pxkr7pzg8n3usx6tyqfst5u966, which is also controlled by xxxkeym.

Shortly before the deposits to Gate, bc1pkkw was funded in three transactions by bc1quzwkggdf6ly06mrrnnled0qdr57w770k45n5n7 & bc1qtu66zfqxj6pam6e0zunwnggh87f5pjr7vdr5cd.

bc1quzw & bc1qtu66z were reported as alibarbit[.]bit, the same scam named in Indian LE's press release. 

That was a mistake. Both belong to the Merlin Chain bridge, which is unlabeled in most compliance tools. 

xxxkeym is simply a normal Merlin user trading tokens on the L2. This wrong label is the only place the scam touches his transaction history.

Below is the blockchain data showing each Merlin withdrawal by xxxkeym matched to a BTC payout from those addresses, plus screenshots of the bridge activity.

xxxkeym bridged 50 BTC into Merlin on March 28, 2024, over a year before the alleged May 2025 theft. 

His three withdrawals came out of that balance. I found zero onchain connections between xxxkeym and the theft.

Separately on July 15, 2025 xxxkeym had a 7 BTC private key compromise theft which was reported to local police and also SlowMist was engaged. His stolen funds flowed to Wasabi. 

This is embarrassing incompetence by Indian LE, who seem incapable of reviewing basic blockchain data.

Indian LE, the prosecutor and the judge all signed off on this, Gate froze the account, and LE did a full press release about it recently, while the real victim here (the Gate user) hasn't had access to his funds for nearly 16 months.

My hot take is VASPs need to challenge weak jurisdictions like India, Canada, etc due to repeated negligence in criminal cases.

AI data-centre: 100% moratorium improbable, modest slowdown likely and it will elongate the cycle (and the selloff has already priced a lot in)

Post-midterm noise has focused on local ballots, state pauses and talk of tighter rules on new data centres. Legitimate friction exists: power, water, permitting and community pushback are real constraints. However, a near-total U.S. halt is improbable as it will send the US into an immediate recession.

AI is a strategic priority; economic and geopolitical costs of freezing buildout are high. Much near-term capacity is already permitted or under construction.

Private land + evolving power solutions (gas, nuclear, efficiency) + international options provide outlets.

No federal ban has material traction; impact is more delay and higher cost than cancellation.

Base case from banks: some 2028 projects slide to 2029. This elongates the AI capex cycle rather than derailing it. Positives include:

1) Smoother supply-demand rebalancing (less boom-bust risk for the supply chain).

2) Better utilisation and pricing power for compute.

3) Improved credit outlook and more sustainable multi-year spending.

4) Hyperscalers still guiding strong near-term capex; and they will likely become FCF +ve

The aggressive selloff in AI infrastructure names (picks-and-shovels, semis, related industrials) has already discounted substantial slowdown risk. Multiples have compressed hard while order books and guidance have stayed firm. This looks more like a positioning/sentiment reset than a fundamental end of the cycle.

Quality AI infrastructure exposure still looks attractive if demand holds. Best to own companies with strong balance-sheets, high margins, FCF and real backlog. https://t.co/YKr5pL7G2c

tweets.text:
Stablecoin holders are giving up about ~$12B a year in T-bill income . That income goes to the issuers.

There should be a switch into these products but the data doesn't show it happening. Since the August peak stablecoins are down $17B and tokenised money market funds are down $2B as well, so money is leaving crypto rather than rotating into yield.

Part of the reason is these funds sit underneath stablecoins as much as beside them. Ethena's USDtb is ~99% backed by BlackRock's BUIDL and its supply has fallen from $877M at the end of Jan to about $350M. When stablecoins shrink, the funds backing them shrink too.

They're also mostly parked. Turnover is under 1x a month, so the back and forth that makes them interesting for a corporate treasury is still more promise than practice.

Until access opens up they're mainly plumbing for stablecoin issuers & trading firms, not yet an alternative for the treasurer sitting on idle stablecoins.

In TradFi, money market funds are an $8T market. Onchain the yield-paying version is $16.6B, 0.2% of that, against $287B of stablecoins paying their holders nothing. Cash naturally drifts to where it earns the bill rate, so that ratio should be multiples higher. That it isn't reflects a market structure that hasn't matured yet (access, plumbing, issuer incentives), and once it does I think these funds end up in the trillions.

Robotics has been constrained by real-world data. Every training example meant doing something in the physical world which is slow and expensive.

Simulation and synthetic data are changing that and robot learning could start moving at the speed of software. Remember, we went from GPT-3.5 fumbling through basic code to Fable 5.2 in less than four years. 

We watched the whole thing happen and still underestimated the rate of progress. My bet is the robotics exponential will be even steeper. Every deployed robot collects more data and so every improvement can reach the entire fleet.

Self-driving cars. Robots across factories. Then multiple robots per home doing the laundry, dishes, cleaning, cooking. Congrats to @theo_gervet and the @gs_ai_ team and please I want one asap

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen
